page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 virtual CPUs across a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio typical of compute-oriented profiles. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512, AES, and FMA. No integrated local storage is bundled, requiring reliance on external block storage, and no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the entry-tier performance bracket compared to broader cloud standards. In CPU benchmarks, the instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 941.0 and a multi-core score of 1114.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1823.49 and stress-ng throughput of 1461.5 operations. Memory bandwidth tests yielded 10.04 GB/sec for large-block sequential reads and 9.48 GB/sec for sequential writes. Network capacity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, facilitating basic ingress and egress data transfer without complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

From a cost-efficiency and operational standpoint, the ecs.c5.large delivers an economical entry point for lightweight compute requirements that do not demand extensive memory or dense multi-threading. Its 1-core, 2-thread allocation and 4 GB memory footprint limit throughput under concurrency, making it less suitable for heavy parallel pipelines or large-scale data manipulation. It is best aligned with lightweight application services, low-traffic web servers, development environments, and modest microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.large is a compute-optimized instance delivering 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of memory on the KVM hypervisor. Built on a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor with a single physical core and two hardware threads, it features a 1:2 memory-to-CPU ratio. The architecture includes AVX-512 support, 33 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, it scored 941.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1114.0 in multi-core, with memory write throughput measuring 9.48 GB/sec. Given its low-concurrency footprint and modest memory allocation, the ecs.c5.large is best deployed for lightweight web serving, microservices, small API endpoints, and staging environments.
